title: Introduction to Machine Learning
description: A first course in machine learning and computational statistics (CCMAS): what machine learning is, data types for learning, supervised and unsupervised learning, statistical learning versus machine learning, linear regression and its output, and classification metrics. Built from Dr O.J. Akintande's STA 122 modules and lecture notes.

topics.title: What Machine Learning Is
topics.summary: Machine learning teaches computers to learn patterns from data, as people learn from experience, so that they can make decisions. The module defines it, places it among related fields, shows the growth of data and lists everyday applications.
subtopics: Definition: learning from experience E at task T measured by P
ML as a subfield of artificial intelligence
Related terms: data science, data mining, statistical learning, KDD

topics.title: Data for Machine Learning
topics.summary: Learning starts with data. The lecture sorts data into categorical (nominal and ordinal), metric (interval and ratio) and the modern TAP classes of text, audio and pictures, and explains training, testing and validation.
subtopics: Categorical data: nominal (binary and non-binary) and ordinal
Modern data classes: text, audio and pictures (TAP)

topics.title: Learning Categories
topics.summary: Machine learning tasks are supervised, where a target Y is learned as a function of features X, or unsupervised, where there is no output. Supervised learning is predictive when Y is metric and classification when Y is categorical.
subtopics: Names for Y and for X
Training and testing a supervised model

topics.title: Statistical Learning versus Machine Learning
topics.summary: Statistical learning focuses on modelling and understanding relationships with interpretable, assumption-based models. Machine learning focuses on prediction accuracy with flexible models on large data. The two are complementary, and the choice involves a trade-off between interpretability and accuracy.
subtopics: Key differences: goal, model, interpretability, data, assumptions, output

topics.title: Linear Regression and Its Output
topics.summary: Regression estimates how a dependent variable changes with independent variables by least squares. The lecture fits umbrellas sold against rainfall in Excel and explains the summary statistics, ANOVA, coefficients, residuals and error measures.
subtopics: Dependent and independent variables; simple and multiple regression
The model Y = β₀ + β₁X + ε and least squares
Running regression in Excel (Analysis ToolPak, LINEST, SLOPE, INTERCEPT, CORREL)
Multiple R, R², adjusted R² and standard error
ANOVA, F and Significance F; coefficients and p-values

topics.title: Classification Metrics
topics.summary: Classification models are judged from the confusion matrix of true and false positives and negatives. From it come sensitivity, specificity, false positive and negative rates, precision, NPV, accuracy and the F1 score, each suited to different costs of error.
subtopics: The confusion matrix: TP, FN, FP, TN
Choosing a metric for the problem
